official.deadline_note: Published in the MSCA Work Programme 2026-2027: HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01 opened 9 April 2026 with deadline 9 September 2026; HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01 opens 7 April 2027 with deadline 8 September 2027 (indicative).
official.status_note: The 2026 call closed on 9 September 2026; the next call is published in the Work Programme 2026-2027 with an opening of 7 April 2027 and deadline of 8 September 2027.
benefits: Living allowance: EUR 6,350 per person-month (a gross amount including compulsory deductions under national law; a country correction coefficient applies)
Mobility allowance: EUR 710 per person-month, covering the researcher's private mobility-related costs (e.g. travel and accommodation costs)
Family allowance: EUR 660 per person-month x % covered by the beneficiary, for researchers who have or acquire family obligations
Long-term leave allowance and special needs allowance, where applicable (requested unit)
Research, training and networking contribution: EUR 1,000 per person-month; management and indirect contribution: EUR 650 per person-month
eligibility: Applicants must hold a doctorate: at the call deadline they must be PhD holders (applications are not accepted after the defence date for those defending)
Maximum 8 years of research experience by the call deadline (counted after the PhD; longer careers are possible for part-time research and family-related breaks)
Mobility rule: applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies) in the host country for more than 12 months during the 36 months before the deadline
European Postdoctoral Fellowships: open to any nationality, 1-2 years in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country
Global Postdoctoral Fellowships: EU nationals or long-term residents, 2-3 years - outgoing phase of 1-2 years in a Third Country plus a mandatory return phase of up to 1 year in Europe
As from 2026, Global Postdoctoral Fellowship applications that score below 80% face restrictions on resubmission (fixed group and similar restrictions apply)
requirements: Applications are submitted electronically via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
The application is joint with the host institution: Part A of the proposal is filled in by the beneficiary (the host institution) and Part B by the researcher
The beneficiary's project supervisor supports the application and supervises the project
Schemes of Excellence: applications scoring 85% and above that are not funded carry the Seal of Excellence 'Excellence - MSCA'
selection_criteria: Evaluation follows the MSCA Work Programme 2026-2027 criteria; call budgets for 2026 were EUR 434.05 million (368.94 for European Fellowships, 65.11 for Global Fellowships) with EUR 459.70 million published for 2027
Schemes of Excellence: funded scores of 85% and above qualify for the Seal of Excellence
coverage: Living allowance of EUR 6,350 per person-month (gross; country correction coefficient applies)
Mobility allowance of EUR 710 per person-month for private mobility-related costs including travel and accommodation
Family allowance, long-term leave allowance and special needs allowance where applicable
Research, training and networking costs (EUR 1,000 per person-month) plus management and indirect costs (EUR 650 per person-month) covered at institutional level
application_method: Find a host institution in an eligible EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and agree the project with the beneficiary's supervisor
Apply electronically via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal within the call's application period
Respect the mobility rule by checking your residence history in the 36 months before the deadline
official.application_route: Apply jointly with your host institution via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal - Part A completed by the beneficiary, Part B by you.
official.study_mode: Full-time; European Fellowships run 1-2 years and Global Fellowships 2-3 years with a mandatory return phase
official.citizenship_residency: European Fellowships: any nationality; Global Fellowships: EU nationals or long-term residents only, with a return phase in Europe
official.international_eligibility: Yes - European Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to applicants of any nationality; Global Fellowships are restricted to EU nationals and long-term residents
official.research_requirement: Applicants must hold a PhD (or defend before the deadline) and have at most 8 years of research experience counted after the PhD
official.duration: European Postdoctoral Fellowships: 1-2 years; Global Postdoctoral Fellowships: 2-3 years (outgoing phase 1-2 years in a Third Country plus a mandatory return phase of up to 1 year in Europe)
official.description: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships fund researchers at doctoral level with a living allowance and mobility allowance, plus institutional research, training, networking, management and indirect contributions, in European or Global fellowship schemes.
official.region: EU Member States, Horizon Europe Associated Countries (European Fellowships); Third Countries globally (Global Fellowships outgoing phase)
official.program_type: EU research and innovation mobility action (Mono-action Postdoctoral Fellowship)

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage (the action page and work programme do not state a tuition item)
documents (not listed on the action page)
verification.notes: Living allowance EUR 6,350 per person-month, mobility allowance EUR 710, family allowance EUR 660, plus EUR 1,000 research/training/networking and EUR 650 management/indirect from the MSCA Work Programme 2026-2027 unit contributions table; call dates (closing 9 Sep 2026; 2027 opens 7 Apr 2027) also from the Work Programme.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fellowship, not a tuition scholarship: the money is a gross salary-like living allowance of EUR 6,350 a month before any country correction, plus EUR 710 a month for your private mobility costs, with the host institution receiving EUR 1,000 per person-month for research and training and EUR 650 for management overhead. Your PhD must be in hand by the deadline, you can be at most 8 years past it, and you cannot have lived in the host country more than 12 of the last 36 months - the mobility rule quietly disqualifies far more people than the degree rule. The 2026 call closed on 9 September 2026, so the realistic target is the 2027 call opening on 7 April 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career PhD holders (0-5 years post-PhD) who can line up a supportive host group across Europe and who have genuinely not worked in that country before.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the mobility rule month by month: no more than 12 months in the host country in the 36 months before the deadline, counting work and studies
Count your research years from the PhD award date and check the 8-year limit, remembering that part-time research and family breaks can extend an eligible career
Choose the scheme deliberately: European Fellowship (any nationality, 1-2 years, no return obligation) versus Global Fellowship (EU nationals/long-term residents, 2-3 years, mandatory return phase)
Agree the project with your host supervisor early, because the host institution must complete Part A of the application
If you are targeting the 2027 call, plan for the 8 September 2027 deadline and note the 2026 call's 434.05 million EUR budget scale
common_rejection_risks: Failing the mobility rule after a prior postdoc, visiting fellowship or sabbatical in the host country
Being more than 8 years past the PhD without accounting for part-time or family-related breaks
Applying for a Global Fellowship without EU nationality or long-term resident status
Weak supervisor letters or a Part B that scores below 85%, which forfeits the Seal of Excellence path
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: No tuition component is published in the action or the work programme unit costs; the allowance is subject to tax and social security deductions and the country correction coefficient, so the net amount varies by host country.
document_audit: Part A is completed by the beneficiary host institution and Part B by you - never let that split slip and produce a missing administrative section
PhD status must be settled by the call deadline, so schedule any defence well before it
alerts: From the 2026 call, Global Fellowship applications scoring below 80% face resubmission restrictions, so a weak application can lock you out of the next round
The 2027 call dates are published but marked indicative in the work programme - confirm them when the call actually opens
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure a host and supervisor, split Part A (host) and Part B (researcher), submit electronically through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal inside the call window, and await evaluation under the published work programme criteria.

official.deadline_note: There is no central application form or central deadline: 'You can reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process', so intake deadlines are institutional.
official.application_cycle: Academic-year intakes arranged by the sending institution and the partner university
official.status_note: Mobility is arranged institution by institution; the official Erasmus+ student exchanges page (last updated 18 December 2025) states there is no central application form and the sending institution is obliged to select applicants in a fair and transparent way.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official page: 'As an Erasmus+ student, you are exempt from fees for tuition, registration, examinations, and charges for access to laboratories or libraries at the receiving institution. Small fees for insurance or student union membership may still apply.'
benefits: As an Erasmus+ student you are exempt from fees for tuition, registration, examinations, and charges for access to laboratories or libraries at the receiving institution; small fees for insurance or student union membership may still apply

The grant amount is a contribution to your travel and daily living costs; the official page says the details depend on differences in living costs between your country and the destination country, the number of students applying for a grant, the distance between countries and the availability of other grants

Programme Guide individual support for long-term mobility: medium range between 292 and 606 EUR per month, higher range between 348 and 674 EUR per month, lower range between 225 and 550 EUR per month; the exact amounts are published on the National Agency and higher education institution websites
Guide base amounts for short-term physical mobility: 79 EUR per day up to the 14th day of activity and 56 EUR per day for the 15th to 30th day of activity
Travel support by distance band: EUR 28 (10-99 km), 211 (100-499 km), 309 (500-1999 km), 395 (2000-2999 km), 580 (3000-3999 km), 1,188 (4000-7999 km) and 1,735 (8000 km or more) for students

Top-ups to the individual support: EUR 250 per month for students and recent graduates with fewer opportunities on long-term mobility, EUR 150 per month for traineeships, and for short-term physical mobility 100 EUR (5-14 days) or 150 EUR (15-30 days)
eligibility: Who can apply: students at short-cycle, Bachelor and Master levels; doctoral candidates registered in a higher education institution participating in the Erasmus+ programme; enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
Your study period abroad must be relevant for your degree-related learning and personal development needs, and part of the study programme you are following

Blended short-term mobility is open to any student, in particular those not able to participate in a long-term physical mobility (for example due to their study field or fewer opportunities); any student may also participate in blended intensive programmes
Total eligible duration: up to 12 months of physical mobility per study cycle; for 'one-cycle' courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months
requirements: Grant agreements are signed by your sending or receiving institution, which applies for funding on behalf of its students; if you are accepted for a grant you sign a participant grant agreement
The sending institution is obliged to select applicants in a fair and transparent way, and the sending and receiving institutions must have an inter-institutional agreement
Institutions in EU Member States or associated countries must also hold the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education
A blended mobility for studies must award a minimum of 3 ECTS credits and include a compulsory virtual component
documents: Learning agreement for studies, signed with your sending and receiving institutions before the study period abroad, which defines how your activities abroad will be recognised and sets the rights and responsibilities of the various parties
Erasmus+ Student Charter, received before departure, explaining your rights and obligations
Transcript of Records, which your receiving institution must give you and your sending institution after the study period abroad, confirming completion and results achieved
coverage: Exemption from fees for tuition, registration, examinations, and charges for access to laboratories or libraries at the receiving institution (small insurance or student union membership fees may still apply)
A contribution to travel and daily living costs: monthly individual support within the Guide's country-group ranges (225-674 EUR per month) plus travel support by distance band
Top-ups for fewer opportunities and traineeships (EUR 250/month and EUR 150/month on long-term mobility; 100-150 EUR on short-term physical mobility)
application_method: Reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process - there is no central application form
Confirm the sending and receiving institutions have an inter-institutional agreement (and hold the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education if in EU Member States or associated countries)
If accepted for a grant, sign the participant grant agreement with the institution, then the learning agreement for studies before departure
official.application_route: Apply through your own university's international or Erasmus+ office - the institution signs the grant agreement and applies for funding on your behalf; never directly to the European Commission.
official.international_eligibility: Open to students registered in Erasmus+ Programme countries (EU Member States, EEA countries and EU candidate countries) at participating higher education institutions
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Mobility follows the agreement between your sending institution and the partner university; the partner academic programme determines what you can study
official.duration: Long-term mobility for studies or traineeships: 2-12 months of physical mobility excluding travel time (including blended mobilities with a virtual component); short-term physical mobility: 5-30 days combined with a compulsory virtual component; doctoral candidates: 5-30 days or 2-12 months; maximum total 12 months per study cycle (24 months for one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture)
official.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from associated countries: students study or train abroad for 2-12 months (or 5-30 days blended) with an EU grant contributing to travel and daily living costs and exemption from the receiving institution's tuition, registration, examination and library fees.
official.region: Erasmus+ Programme countries and countries associated to Erasmus+
official.program_type: Erasmus+ Key Action 1 - learning mobility of individuals (student mobility)

not_confirmed: funding_amount (the Programme Guide publishes ranges by country group - medium 292-606 EUR, higher 348-674 EUR, lower 225-550 EUR per month - plus short-term daily amounts of 79/56 EUR; the exact amounts are set by National Agencies and higher education institutions)
selection_criteria (set institutionally; the page states only that the sending institution must select in a fair and transparent way)
verification.notes: Coverage, who-can-apply, duration and process from the official Erasmus+ 'Studying abroad' page (last updated 18 December 2025); grant ranges, country groups, travel bands, top-ups and short-term daily amounts from the Erasmus+ Programme Guide (2026 Call) higher education mobility funding rules. No single long-term amount is published, so funding_amount stays null.

applicant_utility.summary: Erasmus+ pays you a monthly grant that depends on the country group you are moving to - anywhere between 225 and 674 EUR per month under the Guide's ranges, with the exact figure set by the National Agency and your institution - and exempts you from the receiving institution's tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library access fees. The grant is explicitly a contribution to travel and daily living costs, not a wage: housing deposits, flights and daily life above that contribution are yours to fund. Your application never goes to Brussels; your own university's international or Erasmus+ office applies for the funding on your behalf and also decides your selection.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students at short-cycle, Bachelor and Master levels, and registered doctoral candidates, who can plan 2-12 months abroad and whose institution has a partner agreement.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify that your institution and the target university actually have an inter-institutional agreement in your field before anything else
Contact your international or Erasmus+ office early to learn the annual selection calendar and the monthly rate they apply
Check the monthly support your destination attracts (Group 1 high-cost, Group 2 medium, Group 3 lower living costs) and add the distance-band travel grant on top when budgeting
If you have fewer opportunities, claim the EUR 250/month top-up; if you are doing a traineeship, claim the EUR 150/month top-up

Confirm your level counts: short-cycle, bachelor and master students and registered doctoral candidates are eligible, enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a single Erasmus deadline - each institution runs its own selection calendar and quotas
Leaving before the learning agreement for studies is signed, which voids agreed credit recognition
Expecting the grant to cover the full stay: the official page calls it a contribution to travel and daily living costs
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything above the monthly contribution and travel band: deposit and rent, local transport, insurance and student union fees that may still be charged, and daily living costs - especially if moving from a Group 3 to a Group 1 country.
document_audit: The receiving institution must give you and your sending institution a Transcript of Records after the stay; chase it before your credits are recognised
Your mobility period should be recorded in the Diploma Supplement, depending on where your institution is based - request it after the stay

If you cannot commit to a long-term stay, any student (in particular those with fewer opportunities) can use the 5-30 day blended option with a compulsory virtual component, and a blended study mobility must award at least 3 ECTS credits
alerts: The exact monthly amounts are published only on National Agency and institution websites - get the figure in writing from your own office
Only doctoral candidates can do a short-term mobility without a virtual component
Total physical mobility is capped at 12 months per study cycle, though one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture can reach 24 months
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Confirm the inter-institutional agreement, apply through your institution's international/Erasmus+ office (which applies for the funding), sign the participant grant and learning agreements, spend 2-12 months (or 5-30 days blended) abroad, then collect the Transcript of Records.
